title: LINK TEST: does lifting grazeYieldScale to declared restore grazing flux?

identity.note: The probe always ran from the current checkout. A historical arm spec applied here is a settings replay, not a reproduction of its original figure.

preregistration.hypothesis: Step-0 meter (2026-10-12) showed 66-73% of graze submits resolve with positive takes that the world multiplies by the preset grazeYieldScale=0, so world flux is exactly zero by configuration. Restoring the declared scale (1.0) on the otherwise identical config should restore paying graze wins. Meat stays zeroed by design: one path at a time.
preregistration.prediction: grazeEnergy > 0 on at least 12/18 seeds at tick 6000 (read from per-seed B/D lines; the cohort verifier has no graze metric, so this arm carries no machine criteria and classifies 'not measured' by design — the verdict is human-read from intact evidence, stated here before inspection). Ecological coexistence is explicitly NOT predicted by this arm: it tests the link, not balance.
preregistration.falsification: FALSIFIED as a link restoration if grazeEnergy = 0 on 7 or more of 18 seeds. A falsification here sends the program back to contest biology (defender losses were 27-34% at Step 0), not to a larger scale — do not push to 1.6+ blindly; rung 4 already showed enriched transfer without coexistence.
preregistration.notPredicted: Endpoint guild counts, coexistence rates, and per-win sizes are not predicted. Tissue basis (plantYieldPerMass) is a follow-up only if per-win size disappoints, not part of this arm.
confoundsControlled: Same 18-seed panel, horizon, engine, and lifts as consumer-yield; the ONLY difference is +grazeYieldScale:1.0
Matched comparison against the archived consumer-yield run: any graze flux difference is attributable to the one dial
conservation enforced per seed at 0.5%; a seed above it fails the run rather than reporting
